Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 63f2b1677fba11c5bd02089f25c13421948905f5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Noralf=20Tr=C3=B8nnes?= <noralf@tronnes.org>
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2019 19:18:41 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] staging/fbtft: Depend on OF
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Commit c440eee1a7a1 ("Staging: fbtft: Switch to the gpio descriptor
interface") removed setting gpios via platform data. This means that
fbtft will now only work with Device Tree so set the dependency.

This also prevents a NULL pointer deref on non-DT platform because
fbtftops.request_gpios is not set in that case anymore.

Fixes: c440eee1a7a1 ("Staging: fbtft: Switch to the gpio descriptor interface")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Noralf Trønnes <noralf@tronnes.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190917171843.10334-1-noralf@tronnes.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/fbtft/Kconfig b/drivers/staging/fbtft/Kconfig
index 8ec524a95ec8..4e5d860fd788 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/fbtft/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/staging/fbtft/Kconfig
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
 menuconfig FB_TFT
 	tristate "Support for small TFT LCD display modules"
-	depends on FB && SPI
+	depends on FB && SPI && OF
 	depends on GPIOLIB || COMPILE_TEST
 	select FB_SYS_FILLRECT
 	select FB_SYS_COPYAREA
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/staging/fbtft/Kconfig`**
   - The dependency line for the `FB_TFT` configuration option was modified. 
   - Changed from:
     ```plaintext
     depends on FB && SPI
     ```
     to:
     ```plaintext
     depends on FB && SPI && OF
     ```
   - This change adds a dependency on the `OF` (Open Firmware) subsystem, indicating that the fbtft driver now requires Device Tree support to function properly.

### Relationships

- The modification in the `Kconfig` file establishes a new requirement for the fbtft driver, ensuring that it can only be compiled and used in environments where Device Tree support is available. This change is a direct response to a previous commit (c440eee1a7a1) that altered how GPIOs are managed in the driver, which removed the ability to set GPIOs via platform data. As a result, the driver would not function correctly on non-DT platforms, potentially leading to a NULL pointer dereference. By enforcing the dependency on `OF`, the patch prevents such issues and ensures that the driver is only used in compatible configurations.

Here is the commit message:
staging/fbtft: Depend on OF
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Commit c440eee1a7a1 ("Staging: fbtft: Switch to the gpio descriptor
interface") removed setting gpios via platform data. This means that
fbtft will now only work with Device Tree so set the dependency.

This also prevents a NULL pointer deref on non-DT platform because
fbtftops.request_gpios is not set in that case anymore.

Fixes: c440eee1a7a1 ("Staging: fbtft: Switch to the gpio descriptor interface")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Noralf Trønnes <noralf@tronnes.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190917171843.10334-1-noralf@tronnes.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that the fbtft driver was modified to use the GPIO descriptor interface, which removed the ability to set GPIOs via platform data. This change meant that the driver would not initialize the `fbtftops.request_gpios` function pointer when running on non-Device Tree platforms, leading to a potential NULL pointer dereference when the driver attempted to access this function.

Here is the patch:

 	tristate "Support for small TFT LCD display modules"
-	depends on FB && SPI
+	depends on FB && SPI && OF
 	depends on GPIOLIB || COMPILE_TEST
 	select FB_SYS_FILLRECT

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
- fbtftops.request_gpios = NULL; // Not set on non-DT platforms
```
Reason:
The removal of the ability to set GPIOs via platform data means that on non-Device Tree platforms, the `fbtftops.request_gpios` function pointer is left uninitialized (NULL). When the driver attempts to access this function, it results in a NULL pointer dereference, causing a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+ depends on FB && SPI && OF // Added dependency on Device Tree
```
Reason:
By adding the dependency on Device Tree (OF), the driver ensures that it will only be compiled and used in environments where Device Tree is available, thus preventing the situation where `fbtftops.request_gpios` is NULL and avoiding the potential NULL pointer dereference on non-DT platforms.
